text:
maya: Heads up — CI is failing on the event-validator job for customer-facing audit events. Golden fixtures diffed on 2 events, schema validator threw missing required field 'actor.role'.

samir: ugh. link? job id or failing output?

maya: https://ci.redwood/infrastructure/12345 (shows stacktrace). Here's the failing snippet: 
```
- "actor": {"id": "u-1234"}
+ "actor": {"id": "u-1234", "role": "platform-admin"}
SchemaError: instance is missing required properties (['role']) at /actor
```

kevin: Did we recently change RBAC event shape? I remember the change that added role to role propagation, but that was behind a flag.

eli: I rolled out rbac/propagate-roles two days ago to a small canary. Could be some producers now include role while others don't. That would break golden-fixtures strict equality.

maya: Exactly — some events now include actor.role, some don't. Validator is strict against the golden fixtures we store in /infra/security/golden-events/customer-visible/*.json

ci-bot: build 12345 failed: event-validator → 2 diffs. Full diff uploaded to artifacts (ci.redwood/artifacts/12345/event-validator-diff.txt) :exclamation:

samir: Proposed short fixes: 1) relax schema to make actor.role optional and add validation rule that warns if role missing for production customers, 2) canonicalize golden fixtures to include both variants or use canonicalization before diff (sort keys, remove transient fields).

kevin: I prefer canonicalization + non-deterministic field strip. Right now timestamps and trace_id ordering also cause flaky diffs. For example, we should run: `jq -S 'del(.meta.request_ts, .meta.trace_id)'` before comparison.

maya: Agreed. Also, we need to ensure KMS integration events (kms:key-access) still include actor.identity and key_id — that was another failing sample in the artifacts. Could be a producer bug.

eli: I'll grep the producer logs for the canary rollout and KMS event changes. If producer version >= v2.14 then actor.role should be present.

samir: In the medium-term, add schema migration test: when schema evolves, the CI should run compatibility checks between old golden fixtures and new schema with `--compatibility-strict=false` to allow additive optional fields.

maya: Can someone add a small fixer in the validator pipeline to transform incoming events into the canonical form before diff? Minimal transform: sort keys, remove transient meta fields, default-missing actor.role to null (but keep schema optional). Example script: 
```bash
cat event.json | jq -S 'del(.meta.request_ts, .meta.trace_id) | .actor.role = (.actor.role // null)' > canonical.json
```

kevin: I'll open a PR for that. Also adding a unit test that simulates mixed producers so this doesn't regress.

ops-bot: FYI — added ticket SEC-789 to track a followup: make actor.role optional and canonicalize golden fixtures.

eli: Update — found two producers sending old shape (v2.12) in canary. I'll roll them forward to v2.14 and re-run the validator locally.

maya: Thanks. If rolling forward isn't possible fast, please add a temporary compatibility shim on the validator side; we should avoid breaking customers' CI.

samir: Also, let's add an integration check that runs against a small set of customer-like event sequences, not just single events — ordering and array diffs caused a separate flaky failure last week.

kevin: Noted. I'll add a test harness that normalizes arrays (sort by id) before snapshotting.

maya: OK plan: eli will patch producers or confirm, kevin will PR validator canonicalizer + tests, samir will relax schema with warning logs, ops-bot will track. Re-run CI after PRs.

ci-bot: build 12346 started: event-validator (with patch) — will report back. :rocket:

maya: Thanks team — please @me when you push the validator PR or create a revert if we hit more unknown shapes.

kevin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/event-validator/pull/678 (draft) — includes jq-based normalization and two new unit tests.

eli: Re-run complete locally, golden diffs resolved after normalization. Patching producers scheduled for tonight.

maya: Closing loop: once the patch lands, let's put a small postmortem note in #postmortems with root cause (canary producers & stricter validator) and rollout plan.

samir: Agreed. Short blameless note with action items.

maya: Filing it now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
